Focus on PrivateLink/Private Endpoints vs Transit Gateway peering, region constraints (EU & APAC), IP planning and security controls. Agreement to run pilot in us-west-2 and follow up with technical deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-16T15:00:00Z
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Boreal CTO), Priya Anand (Boreal NetOps), Samir Patel (Boreal Security), Leah O'Neal (Boreal Cloud Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Quick intake on private connectivity options, discuss PrivateLink vs TGW, confirm data residency constraints and pilot region.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, can you hear me okay?
00:08 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Yep, loud and clear, thanks Alex.
00:12 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Great, so quick run of play, I'll do a 10 minute business/context intake, Marta will go into technical connectivity options and then we'll map next steps. If anything is off please interrupt.
00:28 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Hi team, hi Boreal folks, Marta Ruiz from Redwood, SE. We'll focus most on networking but happy to jump to security and pilot ops.
00:40 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): Thanks, quick context from our side: Boreal is migrating two user-facing services to a LLM-backed recommender. We need private inference for PII filtering and residency. Primary regions: eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1, also want a west coast us region for experimentation. Latency requirement for eu is sub 80ms p95.
01:05 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Also, our compliance team requires KMS integration and audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and we need to avoid public egress wherever possible.
01:18 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Understood. A few clarifying questions on traffic patterns: are you expecting high steady throughput or bursty spikes?
01:26 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): It's mostly spiky - batch jobs during nightly syncs and burst during daytime traffic spikes. We estimate 200 req/s peak for inference during promo periods.
01:36 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): From security, we need RBAC, SAML SSO for console access, and host-based allowlists. SOC2 is a must.
01:47 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): We support SAML/SCIM and can integrate with KMS/HSM for key management in Private. We also have audit logs and token-level tracing in the Console - I'll share the whitepaper.
02:02 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Cool. On network, we're trying to understand the tradeoffs: AWS PrivateLink (Private Endpoints) vs Transit Gateway peering vs direct VPC peering.
02:14 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Right - short answer: PrivateLink (AWS NLB+Endpoint Service) gives you private endpoint in your VPC and avoids routing through internet, good for per-account isolation. TGW peering is better for many VPCs behind a hub or cross-account routing. VPC peering is simplest but doesn't scale well for many spokes. Each has IP planning implications.
02:39 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): Are there any special requirements on IP ranges for PrivateLink? We have overlapping /16s in some accounts.
02:47 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): PrivateLink only needs an endpoint elastic IP range in your subnet, but the service load balancer sits in Redwood's account. Overlap is less of an issue than with VPC peering, but we'll need unique target subnets for the endpoint ENIs. If you have overlapping the TGW route approach might be trickier.
03:08 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): What about egress inspection and firewall appliances? We have Palo Alto in-line for some regions.
03:16 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): We can support placing Redwood's Private endpoints behind a NLB and allow traffic from your fw; often customers front the endpoint with their inspection stack. We'll document recommended port ranges and health check IPs.
03:30 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Any differences for GCP/Azure if we eventually use multi-cloud?
03:35 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Yes: GCP uses Private Service Connect, Azure uses Private Link / Private Endpoint. Conceptually similar but different naming and implementation. For now looks like you're AWS-first.
03:46 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Quick check - do you have a preferred pattern? PrivateLink per account or TGW hub-and-spoke?
03:52 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): We prefer hub-and-spoke due to our existing TGW for shared services, but we worry about routing complexity and cross-region costs.
04:03 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): TGW will be costed on transit attachments and data egress - for cross-region you may see inter-region data transfer fees. PrivateLink keeps data within region boundaries between VPCs, cheaper for inter-account within same region. For eu <-> ap you will need regional endpoints or a multi-region strategy.
04:24 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): Data residency: EU workloads must keep payloads in eu-west-1. We can't allow inference to execute outside of the region for EU customers. Is that supported on Redwood Private?
04:35 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Yes, you can pin model versions and instances to region; for Private deployments we can deploy in your chosen region(s). For Hosted you'd be subject to our regional availability but we expose region selection.
04:48 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Ok — good. Tell us about IP allowlisting and how clients authenticate to the private endpoint.
04:55 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Authentication occurs at the application layer using the same Redwood API keys and tokens over the private link; network allowlists are IP-based at the VPC endpoint and can be combined with mTLS for additional assurance. We'll provide the set of IP ranges for our service NLB and health check ranges.
05:14 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): You mentioned mTLS - do you handle cert rotation or we manage?
05:19 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Currently customers handle the certs for mTLS termination inside their VPC. For KMS, Redwood can integrate with your KMS for data-at-rest keys on Private deployments.
05:30 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Marta can share the KMS integration doc and a sample architecture diagram after the call.
05:36 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): On failover, if a region has an outage, can traffic automatically fail to another region while still meeting residency? We need to avoid failing EU traffic to US.
05:48 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Auto-failover across regions would violate residency. We recommend region-limited failover plans: use local fallbacks or degrade to cached responses. Redwood routing policies support region pinning so you can keep eu traffic constrained.
06:03 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): For audit logs, do you push logs to our SIEM or do we pull?
06:09 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Both options. For Private we can stream audit logs to your S3 or Kinesis endpoint, or you can pull from Redwood Console APIs. We'll share event schema.
06:20 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): About the pilot: we want to test with a small fleet first. What does Redwood recommend for a pilot capacity?
06:28 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): For functional validation, a single NLB-backed PrivateLink endpoint in eu-west-1 with a small dedicated pool (e.g., 1-2 GPU instances) should suffice. For load validation we'd scale up. Marta: can you outline sizing options?
06:41 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Sure — we'll propose two configs: dev pilot (1 GPU equivalent, minimal concurrency) and perf pilot (2-4 GPU equivalents, load test harness). We'll include cost delta in the estimate.
06:55 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Jordan, what's your timeline? Procurement windows?
07:00 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): We want pilot in 3 weeks, production in 3 months if pilot goes well. Procurement lead time is ~4-6 weeks for a contract after technical sign-off.
07:10 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): Also, we need to check whether Redwood can sign a DPA with EU data residency clauses.
07:16 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Yes, enterprise legal typically covers that - we'll route to our legal and share the DPA template.
07:22 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): On IP planning - our current CIDR map: prod eu-west-1 10.10.0.0/16, staging 10.11.0.0/16, we have some overlaps in partner accounts. How strict is the no-overlap requirement?
07:36 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): For VPC peering it must not overlap. For PrivateLink it's more forgiving since endpoint ENIs are distinct. TGW also requires careful route pruning if overlaps exist. We'll advise a sanitized CIDR plan for pilot.
07:54 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): One follow up: will we need to open any user-facing ports? We prefer only outbound to the endpoint.
08:01 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): With PrivateLink, you create a private endpoint and initiate outbound calls from your VPC to Redwood - no inbound public traffic. We'll provide exact ports (typically 443) and NLB health check ranges.
08:12 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Let's do a short demo of the Console to show region pinning and model versioning — Marta do you want to share screen?
08:20 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Sure, sharing now. (screen noise) Sorry, looks like I had the wrong tab. Okay, navigating to the Redwood Console — here's the model catalog, you can select region and pin model revisions, here's routing policy UI, and here's the Private > Networking panel where you request a PrivateLink or TGW attachment.
08:48 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): Nice UI. In the Private panel do you show the endpoint IPs or just the instructions?
08:54 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): We show endpoint DNS, recommended subnets, and downloadable CloudFormation/Terraform templates for the endpoint creation. We'll also surface suggested security groups.
09:10 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): What about SNI or TLS hostnames?
09:13 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): The endpoint uses mutual TLS if configured, otherwise standard TLS with certs from our CA. For PrivateLink you get a regional DNS name that resolves to the endpoint.
09:24 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): Ping - any hard limits on number of endpoints or attachments?
09:29 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Soft limits exist; we can raise them per account. We'll capture the expected spokes and pre-request increases for TGW/attachments.
09:40 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Switching to security specifics Samir, you mentioned audit and KMS — any other items we should note?
09:46 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): We want envelope encryption for model artifacts, proof of key custoday, and regular pen tests on the hosting infra. Also need to ensure log retention meets our retention policy (3 years).
09:59 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Redwood Private supports integration with your KMS for keys and can ship logs to your S3/Kinesis. Pen test cadence we can align; many customers run annual pen tests with coordination.
10:12 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): On routing, does Redwood require BGP? Or only static routes via the TGW?
10:18 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): For AWS TGW you typically use static routes in route tables and TGW attachments. If you're using Direct Connect + routers you can leverage BGP at the on-prem edge; Redwood doesn't run BGP into customer networks.
10:32 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): For Direct Connect we will likely front egress via our DX to avoid public internet. Any blockers?
10:38 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): No blockers; customers use DX to reach the TGW hub and then Redwood endpoints in-region. We'll document sample DX/TGW diagrams.
10:50 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): Are there any rate limits or per-connection timeouts we should be aware of?
10:55 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): We expose token-level rate limits; for private we can adjust quotas for pilot. Typical timeouts for streaming calls are configurable but default to 60s for a single response chunk; we'll share specifics.
11:12 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Quick pause — do you want us to run an initial connectivity checklist and upload to your ticketing?
11:18 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): Yes please, open a pilot ticket and CC NetOps.
11:22 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Will do. Marta will you lead the checklist?
11:26 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Yep, I'll own the checklist and include templates.
11:29 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): On success criteria, we'll measure latency p95 < 80ms eu, throughput 200 req/s sustained burst, and no egress to non-EU for EU traffic.
11:42 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Noted. Marta will include those validation tests.
11:47 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): Also want to test key rotation failure modes.
11:50 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): We'll add a key rotation test step.
12:00 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): A random thought — do you support private model hosting inside our VPC (air-gapped) or do we always connect to Redwood-managed infra?
12:11 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Redwood Private can be deployed as a customer-managed package on prem or in your VPC in some configurations, but that's an enterprise project. For this pilot we'll use Redwood-managed private endpoints in our cloud and integrate KMS/log shipping.
12:27 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): That might be needed long term for sensitive workloads, but for pilot managed is fine.
12:33 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Timing — we'll send the docs and diagram today, schedule the deep dive for next Thursday. Is that okay?
12:39 Speaker 4 (Priya Anand): Next Thursday works. Please include timezone UTC+1 for eu folks.
12:44 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Noted. Marta any final technical clarifications before we wrap?
12:49 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Just to confirm: pilot region will be eu-west-1, dev pilot sizing 1 GPU equiv., provide Terraform template for PrivateLink, and list of IP ranges + health checks. We'll run a latency test script during the perf pilot.
13:06 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Yes. Also please include the DPA template for our legal.
13:11 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Will do. Any other questions from Boreal?
13:16 Speaker 5 (Samir Patel): No, thanks.
13:18 Speaker 6 (Leah O'Neal): All good.
13:20 Speaker 2 (Marta Ruiz): Cool, I'll follow up with the network template and the whitepaper.
13:24 Speaker 1 (Alex Chen): Thanks everyone — recap and next steps: Alex will open pilot ticket and send security docs, Marta shares PrivateLink terraform and network checklist, Priya sends CIDR map, schedule technical deep dive next Thursday. We'll reconvene post-pilot to discuss production rollout.
13:42 Speaker 3 (Jordan Lee): Thanks, talk soon.
13:46 End of transcript.
